method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management' (last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed), 44 claims; LICENCE: © The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne; Terms clause 5.2, personal use only; paraphrased and hash-anchored (read at the RCH website Terms and Conditions, clause 5.2). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne 'RCH flowcharts for Seizures - acute management (active seizure flowchart)' (last updated June 2025), 8 claims; LICENCE: © The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne; Terms clause 5.2, personal use only; paraphrased and hash-anchored (read at the RCH website Terms and Conditions, clause 5.2). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 rebuilds the Wave 1 hand-written page (edition 1.0, 2026-09-22), which quoted RCH verbatim, as a paraphrase of the page re-fetched 2026-09-24 (S1) and of the Wave 1 transcription of the active seizure flowchart image (S2). All 52 Wave 1 claims are carried over. The S2 anchors re-check the transcription file, not the image itself: a person should still compare the flowchart steps with the image. The medication claims are now flagged as doses.

claims.claim: **Five headline points:** look for a reversible cause and treat it · most seizures stop within 5 minutes and need no drugs · start drug treatment once total seizure time reaches 5 minutes or is unknown · count pre-hospital benzodiazepine doses in the active plan · teach parents about safety and what to do next time.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Seizures are common:** about 1 child in 20 (5%) has some kind of seizure during childhood, and most are short and stop by themselves, usually inside 5 minutes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Treat straight away** if the duration is unknown or it has gone on for more than 5 minutes, if there is cardiorespiratory compromise, or if there is known pathology (meningitis, hypoxic injury, trauma).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **If the child is still seizing, assess and treat at the same time.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Establish the full duration, pre-hospital time included, and every benzodiazepine dose given just before arrival.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Past history that matters now:** earlier seizures and current anti-seizure medicine (and any management plan) · neurological comorbidity such as a VP shunt or structural brain abnormality · renal failure, which can cause hypertensive encephalopathy · endocrine disease, which can disturb electrolytes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Causes that need their own emergency treatment:** hypoglycaemia · electrolyte disturbance (low sodium, calcium or magnesium) · meningitis · drug or toxin overdose, or envenomation · head trauma · stroke or intracranial haemorrhage.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Under 6 months, a treatable cause is more likely**; think of pyridoxine-dependent seizures.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **History:** a detailed timeline of what happened and how the child behaved before, during and after; hear it from the child where possible, and get a witness account, including any video.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Ask about:** aura or focal features · awareness · recent trauma (consider non-accidental injury) · focal limb or eye movement · the post-ictal phase or hemiparesis · timing against sleep and waking.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Relevant background:** seizures, cardiac disorders or sudden death in the family · features of absence seizures, myoclonic jerks or night-time events · development.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Examination:** a full neurological examination for any abnormality and for signs of raised intracranial pressure or meningitis · heart and circulation, BP included · clues to a cause such as neurocutaneous stigmata or microcephaly · features of a toxidrome (fast heart or breathing, high BP, raised temperature, sweating, diarrhoea, tremor, brisk reflexes).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Red flags:** a head injury followed later by a seizure · developmental delay or regression · headache before the seizure · hypertension · a bleeding disorder or anticoagulant therapy · toxidrome features · focal signs · anything in history or examination suggesting non-accidental injury · arrhythmia, which can cause or follow a seizure (think ECG).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Differential diagnosis:** arrhythmia · breath-holding spell (the episode comes while crying) · vasovagal syncope with an anoxic seizure (on changing posture, after dizziness and nausea) · PNEEs, the paroxysmal non-epileptic events, such as reflux with Sandifer syndrome and gratification disorder (infantile masturbation) · PNES (psychogenic non-epileptic seizures) · benign movements of infancy (shuddering, sleep myoclonus).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **For the first 5 minutes, observe:** most seizures stop without help in that time, so unless the airway is compromised, watching without intervening is appropriate and matches seizure first aid advice.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Allow for benzodiazepines given before hospital** (by parents or paramedics), and make sure no more than 2 appropriate benzodiazepine doses are given in all, pre-hospital doses counted.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Known seizure disorder:** use the child's own seizure management plan if there is one.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid any drug the child is allergic to, or one that has already failed to stop their seizures.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Already taking phenytoin?** Phenobarbitone becomes the alternative second-line drug.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Entry:** is there a suspected causative pathology (check the BGL), cardiorespiratory compromise, or a seizure lasting over 5 minutes or of unknown length? If none, keep the airway open, keep the child safe and watch; if still seizing at 5 minutes, start active treatment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Seizures - acute management (active seizure flowchart)', last updated June 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures-acute-management.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Active treatment:** continuous monitoring and oxygen · venous access · a VBG · a benzodiazepine · treat any causative pathology.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Seizures - acute management (active seizure flowchart)', last updated June 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures-acute-management.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Hard IV access:** give midazolam IM, buccally or intranasally.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Seizures - acute management (active seizure flowchart)', last updated June 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures-acute-management.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Still seizing 5 minutes on:** give the benzodiazepine again and call senior staff.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Seizures - acute management (active seizure flowchart)', last updated June 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures-acute-management.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Still seizing another 5 minutes later:** start a second-line drug, levetiracetam or phenytoin.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Seizures - acute management (active seizure flowchart)', last updated June 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures-acute-management.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Reassess 5 minutes after that infusion ends.** If the seizure continues, give whichever of levetiracetam or phenytoin has not yet been used (phenobarbitone if the child already takes phenytoin), and consider intubation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Seizures - acute management (active seizure flowchart)', last updated June 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures-acute-management.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Reassess again 5 minutes after the second infusion.** If still seizing, get senior help for further seizure management, with airway management if needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Seizures - acute management (active seizure flowchart)', last updated June 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures-acute-management.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Once the seizure stops:** post-seizure care, go back over history and examination, and investigate as needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Seizures - acute management (active seizure flowchart)', last updated June 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures-acute-management.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Midazolam (first line):** IV, IM or IO 0.15 mg/kg, up to 10 mg; buccal or intranasal 0.3 mg/kg, up to 10 mg.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Midazolam formulations:** the injection solution can go by mouth, buccally or intranasally; an oromucosal product also exists, for buccal use only. Intranasal midazolam can sting and irritate the nose.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Diazepam (first line):** 0.3 mg/kg IV or IO, up to 10 mg; the IV route is preferred. ⚠️ Never IM.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Phenytoin (second line):** load 20 mg/kg IV or IO, up to 2 g; give neat or diluted to no weaker than 5 mg/mL, at 1 mg/kg/minute and never faster than 50 mg/minute; needs cardiac monitoring. ⚠️ Do not use in Dravet syndrome.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Levetiracetam (second line):** 40-60 mg/kg IV or IO, up to 4.5 g, diluted to 50 mg/mL and run in over 5 minutes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Phenobarbitone (second line):** 20 mg/kg IV or IO, up to 1 g; at a concentration of 20 mg/mL or weaker, run it in over at least 30 minutes, no faster than 1 mg/kg/minute; needs cardiac monitoring; often used for seizures in neonates.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Valproate (second line):** 20-40 mg/kg, up to 3 g, as one infusion over 3-10 minutes. ⚠️ Avoid under 3 years (high hepatotoxicity risk). Stop at once for a skin reaction, hypersensitivity signs (rash or not), hepatotoxicity or pancreatitis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Pyridoxine (third line):** 100 mg IV; consider it up to 6 months of age when seizures resist standard anticonvulsants.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Refractory seizures needing RSI and ventilation:** infusions may include midazolam, ketamine, propofol or thiopentone, and only with senior staff who are confident with the airway.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Post-seizure care:** recovery position and a maintained airway, watch for further seizures, and investigate where appropriate.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Bloods:** check blood glucose. Consider electrolytes, calcium and a venous gas if a second-line drug was needed · age under 12 months · comorbidity such as a metabolic disorder, diabetes, dehydration or a toxidrome · the child is not back to baseline after the post-ictal phase and any drug effect have passed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **ECG** when an arrhythmia is a possibility.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Consider imaging for:** trauma · a focal seizure · needing a third-line drug · age under 6 months · signs of raised ICP · new focal signs or stroke-like symptoms · a bleeding disorder or anticoagulation · failure to return to baseline, or persisting neurological signs, after the post-ictal phase and drug effects have passed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No CT after a typical seizure in a child with established epilepsy**, unless something else calls for it.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **EEG** is seldom needed acutely and is not routine after a first seizure; consider it under 12 months of age or with a known genetic condition.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **The commonest causes of afebrile seizures in children** are SeLECTS (self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes, also called BFEC, CECTS or benign rolandic epilepsy) and IGE (idiopathic generalised epilepsy). An EEG confirms them, but they may need no treatment, so it is rarely urgent; an EEG is generally done after a second seizure, and a confirmed diagnosis can spare neuroimaging.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Discuss with the local paediatric team:** age under 12 months · possible infantile spasms · a prolonged seizure · recovery that is not complete · meningoencephalitis or other intracranial pathology · focal seizures or focal post-ictal findings · repeated seizures without an epilepsy diagnosis · frequent or uncontrolled seizures in known epilepsy · developmental delay · other comorbidities · concern about non-accidental injury.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Admit for observation** if under 12 months.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Tertiary transfer** for a child expected to need ICU-level care because of cardiorespiratory compromise.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Discharge** an older child who is back to baseline function and has no red flags in the history or on examination.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Teach every family before discharge:** the recurrence risk · seizure safety · first aid and the management plan · filming events when it is safe, and keeping a record · written information · whether emergency medication (buccal midazolam) is needed · driving advice for older children old enough to drive.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **After a first afebrile seizure, every child needs medical follow-up.** EEG is not routine but should be considered under 12 months or with a known genetic condition.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **PIC endorsed; last updated June 2025.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Second-line trials cited:** ConSEPT (Dalziel et al., Lancet 2019;393) and EcLiPSE (Lyttle et al., Lancet 2019;393), each testing levetiracetam against phenytoin in children with convulsive status epilepticus, and ESETT (Chamberlain et al., Lancet 2020;395), comparing levetiracetam, fosphenytoin and valproate by age group.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Other references:** the AMH Children's dosing companion · APLS seventh edition (2024) · NICE NG217 (2022) · the ILAE classification of childhood-onset epilepsy syndromes (Epilepsia, 2022) · status epilepticus or seizure guidelines from Queensland (QPEC), SA Health, WA (Perth Children's Hospital), the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network and Starship (NZ).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Seizures - acute management', last updated June 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Seizures_-_acute_management/, retrieved 2026-09-24
